why: A whole Tally XML export, held as JSON strings rather than TypeScript template literals ON PURPOSE: a literal CRLF inside a template literal is at the mercy of the editor, of prettier and of git autocrlf, so the fixture that exists to prove line endings are normalised would be the first thing silently rewritten to LF -- and it would still pass. JSON escapes survive all three. Every date here is in 2026 or 2027, so no value can coincide with the real clock. AND THE ORDERS DISAGREE WITH THE ANSWERS, in three separate ways: Vouchers.xml comes BEFORE Masters.xml, so every ledger a voucher names is introduced after the voucher; inside Masters.xml the group Karnataka Customers is written after the ledger that hangs under it; and the vouchers are in neither date order nor number order. An importer that resolved anything during its walk, or that sorted on the way through, disagrees with the expected output rather than passing by luck.

Vouchers.xml.why: Eleven vouchers and one COMPANY element nobody claims, in an order that is neither by date nor by number. It declares ISO-8859-1, which the XML reader reports and cannot check. The last voucher sits DIRECTLY under REQUESTDATA with no TALLYMESSAGE around it, which is a shape real exports have and which a path-based predicate would miss. PB-2027-018 writes its entries under LEDGERENTRIES.LIST, one amount as <Amount> in mixed case, and one with a currency symbol and Indian grouping. CS-2027-007 is a voucher type the company invented -- ordinary in Tally -- and it is an otherwise perfectly good sale, so adding one row to the voucher-type table imports it.

ambiguousEntryList.why: One voucher writing its entries under BOTH ALLLEDGERENTRIES.LIST and LEDGERENTRIES.LIST. Adding them together would post the voucher twice over; taking the first would make the answer depend on which name elements.ts lists above the other. Neither is a decision to take on somebody else books.

noParty.why: A voucher naming no party and holding no ledger under a customer or supplier group. There is nobody to bill.

namedPartyWithNoEntry.why: PARTYLEDGERNAME naming a ledger that is on none of the entries. Every entry would become a line, including the one that is really the party side.

partyNameDisagreesWithChain.why: PARTYLEDGERNAME left stale after a ledger was renamed. The chain wins because the chain is a fact about the chart; the disagreement is still reported.

unreadableDates.why: Three vouchers: one date in a format Tally does not write, one impossible day, one missing date element. Each is reported separately and none of them stops the fourth voucher from importing.

unreadableEntry.why: An entry whose amount is not a number, and one with no ledger name. Each takes its whole voucher with it, because dropping one entry leaves a voucher that no longer balances.

renamedElements.why: An export whose voucher number is written under a name this build does not know. The document is refused for having no number, the unread element is reported BY NAME, and one correction reads the file -- which is the whole answer to "what if an element name in this folder is wrong".

mixedCaseElements.why: The same voucher with every tag in mixed case, which is what a file that has been through a connector or a template looks like. XML is case-sensitive; elementKey is what makes this one voucher rather than none.

optionalVoucher.why: An optional voucher, which Tally itself does not post. Reported and left out, beside an ordinary one that is imported.

documentWithoutNumber.why: A sales voucher with no number beside a payment with no number. The document is refused because its number is its identity and goes into its fingerprint; the voucher is kept because a voucher number is allotted by whichever program recorded the money and is deliberately not in one.

zeroEntryWithFlag.why: A zero-amount entry, once with ISDEEMEDPOSITIVE and once without. Zero is neither negative nor positive, so the sign says nothing and the flag is the only signal there is; with no flag the entry has no side at all.

identicalReceipts.why: Two receipts from one customer, on one day, for one amount, with no bank reference. They fingerprint identically and they are two real payments.

duplicateGuid.why: Two ledgers carrying one GUID, which is what a merged company file looks like. One of them would be silently lost at write time, and which one depends on the order the writer iterates in.

replacementCharacters.why: A file decoded with the wrong codec, so U+FFFD stands where letters should. The XML reader reports it and this importer carries the report into the batch.

blankCandidateBesideAValue.why: A voucher that writes an EMPTY <REFERENCE/> beside a <REFERENCENUMBER> that carries the bank reference. Both are candidates for one field, and an empty one is ABSENT rather than a second value -- otherwise the ordinary export, which fills in one of a pair and leaves the other blank, would be reported as ambiguous on every voucher it has.

repeatedUnclaimedElement.why: ONE ledger carrying TWO elements of a name no field claims. Without this row the count in an unclaimed report is only ever the number of LEDGERS that carried one, so a per-element counter that never increments reads exactly the same.
